classifications.reason: The contract describes human-powered devices, which are expressly excluded from the vehicle category required by the moped definition.
Neither the bus contract nor the admitting words impose a two-wheel minimum, so an admitted member need not satisfy the covering class's two-or-three-wheel requirement.
The contract describes a person, whereas the moped definition admits a kind of vehicle device.
Commercial mass or licensing does not establish two or three wheels, while the admitting words permit fewer wheels than the covering contract requires.
The contract's bicycle with an assisting motor retains human-powered propulsion, which the vehicle definition excludes independently of the express statutory electric-bicycle exclusion.

The defined electric-scooter exception requires the 100-pound and 20-mph limits, but the class contract requires neither and therefore can describe scooters outside that exception that the moped language admits.
Emergency designation supplies no two-or-three-wheel restriction, so it does not establish that every admitted member satisfies the quoted ru.moped contract.
The fire-fighting vehicle contract supplies no wheel-count restriction that closes the gap between the definition's maximum of three wheels and the covering contract's requirement of two or three.
The express moped definition admits the jurisdiction-classified, low-power two- or three-wheelers described by this contract.
Excluding separately classified powered two-wheelers does not exclude one-wheelers, which the admitting words can reach but the ru.moped contract does not cover.
Every admitted member has two or three wheels under its own contract and satisfies the jurisdiction's moped definition, establishing membership in the proposed covering class.
Official service and identifying equipment do not require two or three wheels, so the covering contract does not account for every member the admitting words can reach.
The contract describes persons rather than the vehicle devices admitted by the moped definition, including when those persons use wheelchairs or assistive devices.
A pedestrian carrying a cane or receiving guidance remains a person rather than a vehicle device admitted by the definition.
The contract's on-track equipment need not be used exclusively upon stationary rails, so the quoted exception does not exclude every member the admitting words could reach.
School-bus designation and markings impose no two-or-three-wheel requirement, leaving the proposed coverage incomplete for members admitted with fewer wheels.
The passenger-for-hire contract imposes no wheel count, whereas the proposed covering class requires two or three wheels and the admitting definition does not.
Neither branch of this contract establishes the two-or-three-wheel requirement needed to place every admitted member in ru.moped.
The drawn-vehicle or combination contract supplies no two-wheel minimum, so it does not establish complete coverage by the narrower ru.moped contract.
Public-transit service and identifying displays do not establish two or three wheels, leaving admitted members outside the demonstrated scope of the covering contract.
A goods-carrying body does not establish two or three wheels, so the definition's maximum wheel count cannot prove coverage by ru.moped.
